Description

The Holbrook Team and Colorado Parks and Wildlife (CPW) are recruiting a Research Scientist to join them at the University of Wyoming (work location will be in Laramie, WY). The Research Scientist will primarily be working at the intersection of elk behavioral ecology and human recreation. We have deployed an extensive network of trail counters and cameras, as well as GPS units to recreationists, to sample human recreation. We have also acquired privatized human mobility data to add to our sample of humans recreating on our landscapes of interest.  Additionally, over the last 6 years, our team has deployed GPS collars on 280 adult female elk in the two main study locations. The main objective for this position is to advance our understanding regarding human-elk interactions, and provide guidance on recreation development into the future. Recreation is multi-billion dollar economy, and generating insights that inform the development conversation for wildlife conservation is really our hope with this position. 

See the following webpages for more information on the Holbrook Team (https://sites.google.com/site/josephdholbrook03/) at the University of Wyoming. 

Candidates should have expertise in a suite of modeling approaches aimed at understanding animal-habitat relationships and animal movement.  Candidates should show creativity and flexible thinking, be extremely self-motivated, and have an authentic desire to cultivate real-world insights from data analyses. Candidates should also be able to work exceptionally well with a team of collaborators. 

The position is for one to three years, with appointment for the second year and beyond contingent on performance and project funding. Financial support for travel to attend at least one conference will also be available.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:  
·         Lead research projects related to advancing our understanding of elk-human recreation relationships;
·         Publish work in peer-reviewed journals and present at conferences;
·         Mentor graduate students;

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:  
·         Masters of Science degree is required for this position;
·         MS in a related field (ecology, wildlife ecology);
·         Experience collaborating and/or being part of a team;
·         Strong written and oral communication skills (English)
 DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:  
·         Experience with models seeking to address animal-environment relationships using GPS-based data; 
·         Experience with animal movement modeling with the aim of informing animal-environment relationships; 
·         Experience with spatial data in R;
·         Familiarity with Wyoming and/or the rural intermountain west

REQUIRED MATERIALS:  

Complete the online application and upload the following for a complete application: 

·         Cover letter/narrative (max. 1 page) that explains your desire to pursue work in elk-human recreation ecology, your research interests, career goals, and highlights relevant experience; Resume or CV including degree(s) earned, GPA, and contact information for at least three references (references will not be contacted until after preliminary interviews); and a writing sample (for example, a first-authored manuscript you have written). 

This position will remain open until filled. Applications will be reviewed upon being received. 
 Questions can be directed to Search Committee Chair Joe Holbrook (Joe.Holbrook@uwyo.edu). 

Contact
Joe Holbrook
Joe.Holbrook@uwyo.edu (preferred contact method)

Description
 THE ROLE

Wildlife Innovations is building a bench of experienced avian biologists we can call on for nesting bird surveys, preconstruction avian surveys, nest and burrow monitoring, and compliance monitoring for sensitive and special-status species across coastal Southern California. Assignments are matched to your availability and to project schedules; there is no minimum hours commitment. 

This is a flexible, project-based role well suited to a biologist who wants variable hours, the ability to pick up assignments around an existing schedule, and potential opportunities for specialized training. Further, biologists who demonstrate exemplary performance may be offered the chance to join the Wildlife Innovations’ full-time team. 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

•    Conduct preconstruction and nesting bird surveys, adhering to the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, California Fish and Game Code, and project-specific permit conditions 

•    Identify Southern California birds by sight and sound, including raptors, corvids, shorebirds, and the special-status species relevant to each site 

•    Locate, flag, age, and/or monitor active nests; establish and enforce mitigation measures (when applicable) and communicate results in real time to project biologists and construction crews 

•    Monitor burrows (e.g., burrowing owl) for occupancy, and support monitoring for California Least Tern, Western Snowy Plover, and other special status species as needed 

•    Collect georeferenced field data digitally and contribute to technical survey summary reports 


This list is representative, not exhaustive; additional duties may be assigned. 


ABOUT WILDLIFE INNOVATIONS

We are a DGS-certified small/micro business specializing in wildlife research, monitoring, and management. Our mission is to support the protection and recovery of listed species, help clients maintain environmental compliance, rescue injured and contaminated wildlife, and mitigate risks to human health and safety. We work across active construction sites, airports, military installations, ports, and state and city parks, with most of our staff cross-trained across various projects, including those requiring specialized training and certifications. 

Our work is grounded in understanding the relationships between species in local ecosystems and the stressors created by human modification of the landscape. We use advanced monitoring and surveillance techniques to design strategies that resolve wildlife conflicts, reduce impacts during construction, improve management outcomes, and support the recovery of focal species. 


QUALIFICATIONS

Description

Organizational Mission:

The Appalachian Trail Conservancy’s mission is to protect, manage, and advocate for the Appalachian National Scenic Trail.


Position Summary


ATC Ridgerunners provide information about the A.T. and its intended primitive experience, location, regulations, and traditions. They work to encourage the best behavior on the part of hikers to facilitate a positive Trail experience (particularly for those who are poorly prepared), and to elicit the support of those who live nearby. They discourage and mitigate misuse of the Appalachian Trail and its environments by performing educational and public-relations functions. 

Ridgerunners are assigned to hike specific sections of the A.T. during the day and camp at specific, high-use overnight sites throughout their patrol. Applicants should demonstrate the interest and ability to contribute to the public service effort of working on a National Scenic Trail and to promote volunteerism and membership in ATC and its club affiliates. They should possess the required skills listed below and be able to attend required trainings. Applicants must demonstrate maturity, responsibility, initiative, and self-motivation.  


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Meet and greet the public and educate them about the A.T., the ATC, local Trail Clubs, local land agencies and Leave No Trace practices.
Advise visitors on rules and regulations pertinent to the A.T. in the Smokies, including general backcountry and thru-hiker permits, proper food storage, and when relevant, parking tag requirements.
Perform minor Trail maintenance which includes but not limited to, picking up litter on the Trail, overnight sites, and at Trailhead parking areas.
Assist with privy maintenance as needed. 
Assist visitors, and when necessary and able, aid in emergency response incidents.
Report unsafe conditions, misuse, and abuse of the A.T. and its overnight facilities.
Maintain regular contact with field supervisors, Club volunteers, agency partners, and local officials.  
Complete a summary report at the end of each work period and attend a weekly debrief call with supervisors and partners.
Regularly traverse steep and uneven terrain in all weather conditions, traveling upwards of 15 miles daily, while carrying approximately 30 pounds.

Qualifications

Commitment to Trail and resource protection efforts.
Proven ability to work alone with minimal supervision.
Ability to effectively communicate with individuals and groups.
Strong backpacking and outdoor experience.
Experience in working with volunteers of all ages, backgrounds, and skill levels.
Ability to hike up to 10 miles per day in steep, mountainous terrain.
Basic knowledge of Long Trail/Appalachian Trail system preferred.
Leave No Trace Trainer or Master Educator desirable, but training provided.
Current First-Aid and CPR certification (Wilderness First-Aid certification is preferable) training can be provided.
Previous A.T. volunteer experience is a preferred.
Physical Demands and Work Environment

Regular use of a computer is required; Microsoft Office, Office 365, ESRI GIS, NPS database and Google applications are used.
May be exposed to hazardous physical conditions and seasonal exposure to extreme weather conditions, including rain, snow, humidity, intense heat, and sunlight.
Must be able to hike for extended periods, stand for long periods, perform routine moderate lifting, carry up to 50 pounds in a backpack over a minimum of five miles, traverse rough, uneven terrain and wet and slippery surfaces.
Living and performing work in the backcountry for multiple days and overnights.
Must have valid driver’s license. Access to a personal vehicle is strongly preferred.
Possible exposure to ticks and pests, extreme weather, and hazards typical of a backcountry environment
Long days in the field and weekend work, typically 40 hours per week

Additional Details:

Ridgerunners working in Georgia will work a 12-week season beginning in early February. 
In-person training will begin Monday February 1st, 2027. Any remote training components that take place prior to the in-person training will be communicated ahead of time. 
The last day of the season will be Monday April 19th, 2027.
Free housing is provided on-site at Amicalola Falls State Park.
Hourly Rate: $19.00 - $21.00
Benefits: 1 hour of sick time per 30 hours worked.

Description
THE ROLE

The Predator Biologist conducts and/or oversees surveillance, research, and targeted management of high threat predators of special status species, including but not limited to nesting California Least Terns and Western Snowy Plovers, in coastal San Diego, Orange, and/or Los Angeles Counties. This is applied and adaptive conservation work, with the data collected used to help steer management efforts both locally and regionally, with the goal of developing and implementing innovative equipment and techniques to increase program efficiency, reduce negative impacts to native predator populations, and achieve recovery goals. 

Day-to-day operations will be based on predator and prey activity, driven by diurnal and nocturnal physical and digital surveillance of nesting and adjacent areas and post-predation site investigations. Active management of high-threat individuals may include a variety of non-lethal and lethal tactics tailored to the species, behavior, and permit conditions. All activity will be digitally collected and analyzed for technical reporting and further development of the programs. Work may include development and testing of experimental techniques to address special status species conflict and GPS tracking of predator movements. Additionally, some work may require injured and contaminated wildlife recovery and transport, as part of on-call rescue projects or oil spill response. 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

•    Conduct diurnal and nocturnal predator surveillance and monitoring, through general and protocol-level surveys, identifying potential and confirmed high-threat predators (to species, age, and sex, when possible) and their behavior 

•    Deploy, operate, and maintain cellular trail cameras and other surveillance equipment; download, review, and log data for integration into active management efforts and technical reporting 

•    Investigate predation events and use evidence to support identification of high-threat individuals or species 

•    Implement targeted management of high-threat predators using a variety of lethal and nonlethal tactics, in compliance with company protocols and federal, state, and site-specific regulations 

•    Record data digitally, maintain project databases, and prepare weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual technical reports 

•    Support ongoing predator research, including development and/or refinement of innovative surveillance and management techniques, and assist with injured wildlife recovery and transport 


This list is representative, not exhaustive; additional duties may be assigned.


ABOUT WILDLIFE INNOVATIONS

Wildlife Innovations (WI) is a DGS-certified small business specializing in wildlife research, surveillance, monitoring, and management. WI provides support for a variety of tasks, such as listed species protection and recovery, environmental compliance, wildlife rescue, hazing, and transport, human health and safety, and conflict and damage mitigation. Our work spans across a diverse set of landscapes, including construction sites, airports, military installations, ports, and state and city parks and beaches. Our approach is grounded in the relationships between species in local ecosystems and the stressors created by human modification of the landscape; for this, we use a combination of historic and advanced monitoring, surveillance, and management techniques to help resolve wildlife conflicts, improve outcomes, and support the recovery of focal species. Most staff are cross-trained across multiple projects and techniques to provide more adaptive and expedited responses 
 QUALIFICATIONS 
 | Required •    Bachelor's degree or higher in Wildlife Science, Biology, or a closely related field from an accredited university •    Three or more years of applicable field experience (the mix of avian versus mammalian experience may adjust this requirement) •    Proficiency in the safe handling, transport, and maintenance of firearms; firearms experience must be recent (within 12 months); applicants without this will not be considered •    Accurate identification of Southern California predators, especially birds of prey, corvids, and mammals, by sight, sound, and track, to species, age, and sex (required) •    Extensive trapping and/or hunting experience, including operating, maintaining, transporting, constructing, and deploying a range of wildlife traps •    Animal tracking experience; ability to safely handle a variety of wildlife species; experience with physical and digital surveillance equipment •    Experience conducting wildlife surveys, logging detailed field data, and preparing technical reports; strong written and oral communication •    Extensive four-wheel-drive experience on steep, muddy, or sandy terrain, and basic vehicle maintenance (fluids, tire pressure, changing a tire) •    Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, SharePoint); valid California driver's license, or the ability to obtain one on hire | Preferred: Highlight any that apply •    Experience conducting predator control within sensitive-species habitat, and conducting predation investigations •    California trapping license; hunter education certificate and hunting license; NRA Firearms Safety Instructor certification; ammunition reloading •    Currently listed on, or holder of, a CDFW Scientific Collecting Permit, Master Banding Permit, or other active California wildlife permit; banding, tagging, or raptor-marking experience; GPS transmitter deployment •    Project management experience leading and scheduling field teams and coordinating with clients across multiple sites, ideally on wildlife management projects •    Project procurement and development experience •    Experience consulting with state and federal regulatory agencies, and preparing, maintaining, and reporting on permits •    Primary authorship of annual reports, proposals, and management plans; CEQA/NEPA document preparation; environmental compliance experience •    FAA Part 107 certificate with UAS survey or monitoring experience; ArcGIS or other mapping proficiency; California Boater Card •    MS in Wildlife Science or a related field •    Experience in Ai coding and image recognition software

Description
Florida International University’s Freshwater Resource Division at the Institute of Environment is seeking to fill a Postdoctoral Associate position to examine the population and community responses of wetland animals (e.g., fish, crayfish, insects, wading birds) to water level variation and other stressors (e.g., fish invasions).  The position will be focused on time series analyses of fish and macroinvertebrate communities using datasets spanning > 29 years.  The 100% research position will include some fieldwork (perhaps 30-40 days per year), leadership in project development, and modeling of population or community time series data.  Complementary experimental, modeling or observational studies will be possible depending on the specific interests of the successful applicant and available funds.  The selected candidate will be expected to be an interactive and collaborative member of a large aquatic ecology lab at FIU and will and work closely with Dr. Dorn, the graduate students and lead technicians. There may also be opportunities to collaborate with other labs at FIU associated with the Institute of Environment or the FCE LTER. The successful candidate will minimally take lead authorship publishing from datasets already existing in the lab and could be asked to contribute to annual reports and assessments of animal responses to Everglades restoration.    

The position has funding for up to two years (salary and faculty benefits), with annual renewal contingent upon performance and continued fit with the needs of the lab. The position is immediately available for a motivated and intellectually curious applicant with proven quantitative, problem-solving, collaborative, and communication (written and oral) skills. 

The position will be located in North Miami, FL on the Biscayne Bay Campus of Florida International University and field work will occur in the Everglades and adjacent wetlands in southern Florida. 

A Ph.D. in Ecology, Fisheries or a related field and prior publications will be required at the time of employment.  The candidate should broadly be interested in species interactions and population/community ecology in aquatic systems.  Experiences conducting field experiments and statistical analyses of time series or spatial surveys are desirable.  Ideal starts are between January and May of 2027. 

We are especially interested in applicants who share a commitment to high standards for science, curiosity about both basic and applied ecological questions, and development of new tools for community and ecosystem monitoring. We encourage candidates from under-represented groups to apply.  

Applicants should send a cover letter, CV and list of references directly to Dr. Nathan Dorn (ndorn@fiu.edu).  Review of applications will begin in mid-November and the position will remain open until filled.

FIU is a member of the State University System of Florida and an Equal Opportunity, Equal Access Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Description
Azura is seeking a Bycatch Analyst to support the NOAA Fisheries Northeast Fisheries Science Center (NEFSC) Protected Species Division (PSD) which conducts research on protected species (cetaceans, pinnipeds, sea birds, marine turtles, and anadromous fish) that live or migrate off the coast of the northeastern United States (U.S.). This work requires professional knowledge of protected species and habitats and environmental compliance requirements related policies, such as the  Endangered Species Act (ESA), Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA), National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (MSA).
 Having high attention to detail and the ability to manage short project timelines are critical skills for this position. Potential candidates must also possess the ability to manage a project to its completion. Applicants must be able to operate independently, manage their own work schedule, and dedicate blocks of time for uninterrupted focus, while effectively working and communicating with collaborators to meet project objectives.
 Place of Performance and Work Schedule
The preferred place of performance is the Woods Hole, Massachusetts area or a remote location within the U.S. During workdays, candidates must be able to respond to all communications within 24 hours and conduct calls and meetings as necessary during normal business hours. Work is full-time (40 hours per week, Monday through Friday) and expected to last one year with the possibility of extension. The estimated start date is October 1, 2026 (pending security investigation). Travel is anticipated to occur one to two times per year. This position is not open to visa sponsorship or relocation assistance.
 Compensation and Benefits 
Rate: $37.13/hour
Competitive benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; 401k with employer match; life and disability insurance; and paid time off for vacation, sick leave, and company-observed holidays. 
 Duties
The employee will perform a variety of tasks related to the position. Specific tasks may include the following primary and secondary duties.
 Primary:
Prepare standard annual bycatch estimates of all species of small cetaceans and pinnipeds encountered in U.S. Atlantic gillnets and bottom trawls (and potentially other gear types) by using existing code and importing new data annually, including preparation of annual Center Reference Documents documenting the estimates and methods, and providing these analyses for incorporation into the annual marine mammal Stock Assessment Report.
Prepare periodic estimates of sea turtle interactions with different gear types and prepare Center Reference Documents reporting the estimates and methods.
Perform extensive auditing of fisheries data to support bycatch estimation.
Conduct bycatch and other analyses needed to inform the Harbor Porpoise Take Reduction Team (HPTRT) and present findings to the Team.
Prepare annual gillnet observer allocation in close coordination with the Northeast Fisheries Observer Program (NEFOP).

Secondary:
Provide bycatch information for the annual State of the Ecosystem reports.
Maintain awareness of observer activity and advise on reallocation of gillnet observers, if appropriate.
Contribute to sturgeon bycatch analysis and support Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (ASMFC) sturgeon stock assessment bycatch data requests.
Contribute to seabird bycatch hotspot analysis and support NEFSC-FWS seabird data requests.
 Required Qualifications
Education and/or experience in the application of statistical methods to the biological sciences, with an advanced degree (e.g., Master’s) in fisheries, marine biology, statistics, or a related field preferred.
Three to five years of relevant professional experience demonstrating the competencies described above, preferably in fisheries, marine science, or a related field.
Ability to independently plan, organize, and carry out work projects within schedule and budgetary constraints.
Experience using statistical analysis software (e.g., R) and working with existing codebases.
Ability to identify and resolve issues in R code and implement extensions or enhancements.
Ability to effectively present findings to audiences with varying technical backgrounds.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Word, and PowerPoint) and Google Workspace.
Eligibility to work in the U.S.
Candidate must be able to obtain a Public Trust Clearance which requires passing a thorough background check. 
 Preferred Qualifications
Education or experience related to fisheries data and fisheries biology.
Experience with Oracle databases and SQL.

Job Description:
The Center for Wildlife Sustainability Research at Southern Illinois University is seeking multiple Deer Research Technicians and Lead Technicians to assist with white-tailed deer research across Illinois. This project is conducted in collaboration with the Illinois Department of Natural Resources and focuses on white-tailed deer movement, disease ecology, and population density estimation.

These positions provide extensive hands-on experience with wildlife capture and handling, GPS telemetry, biological sampling, camera trapping, and multiple approaches to estimating deer abundance. Technicians will serve as the primary field staff for the project and work closely with SIU graduate students, project staff, partnering agencies, landowners, and volunteers.

Primary responsibilities include:

Capture and collaring of deer via clover traps, drop nets, and dart guns
Handling and processing captured deer, including:
GPS collar fitting
Disease sampling
Blood drawls
Nasal and oral swabs
Ear tag and ear biopsy
Morphometric measurements
Age and body condition assessments
Conducting nighttime deer density road surveys using vehicle-mounted forward-looking infrared (FLIR) cameras
Deploying and retrieving large-scale camera grids
Scouting, baiting, and preparing deer capture sites
Checking trap lines and monitoring drop-net and darting sites
Mortality investigations
Processing biological samples in the lab, including centrifuging blood, pipetting plasma and serum.
Entering, organizing, and conducting QA/QC of field data
Maintaining and repairing traps, capture equipment, cameras, and other field gear
Maintaining professional relationships with private landowners, volunteers, and partnering agencies
 Timeline:
We anticipate hiring six positions beginning November 18, 2026 (four technicians and two lead technicians) and two additional technician positions beginning January 4, 2027. Preference for the November positions will be given to applicants who can work the full field season. The January positions will begin with deer capture operations and are expected to continue through the spring FLIR survey and camera retrieval period.

Applicants who are available for the capture period but cannot remain through the spring survey period may still be considered, particularly if they have substantial relevant experience with large-mammal capture and handling. Please clearly indicate your preferred start date and availability in the body of your application email.

November 18 – December 22, 2026: Deer density surveys and camera deployment
Technicians will be divided between two crews operating in northwestern and northeastern Illinois. Work will primarily consist of nighttime FLIR road surveys, deployment of camera grids, and associated field work. This portion of the position will involve substantial driving and hiking. Technicians should expect to work through Thanksgiving.

December 23, 2026 – January 3, 2027: Holiday break
All crews will receive a scheduled 12-day break over the Christmas and New Year period.

January 4 – March 31, 2027: Deer capture season
Technicians will transition to two capture crews operating in central and southern Illinois. This will be the capture-intensive portion of the position and will include clover trapping, drop-netting, remote darting, deer handling and processing, biological sampling, GPS collar deployment, and associated field and laboratory work.

April 1 – April 24, 2027: Deer density surveys and camera retrieval
Crews will conduct a second round of FLIR surveys and retrieve camera grids following the capture season.

The exact end date is somewhat flexible and will depend on capture progress, survey schedules, and individual technician hours. Positions are expected to conclude between mid-March and late April 2027, or when the maximum appointment limit of 900 hours is reached.

Location:
Multiple sites in Illinois.

Salary:
Base pay starting at $16.00/hour but commensurate with experience. Lead technicians start at $18/hour. 

Housing is provided throughout the duration of the position.

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications: 
 Applicants should have academic training in wildlife or related field. Must be willing to work long hours in the field, performing physically strenuous tasks outdoors in adverse weather conditions, including extreme cold at times (trapping equipment weighing >50lbs needs to be moved regularly, and adult deer must be physically restrained before anesthesia is administered). Must have prior experience in off-road driving 4-wheel drive vehicles. Required qualifications also include an enthusiasm for outdoor work with wildlife, getting along with your crewmates, reading maps and navigating independently (sometimes without cellular service), demonstrate organizational and communication skills, attention to detail, ability to follow study protocols, and carefully record data. Driver’s license required.
 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Highly qualified applicants will have prior experience in large mammal and/or adult deer captures, radio telemetry, chemical immobilization, mortality investigations, and camera trapping.

Lead technician applicants should meet most preferred qualifications, plus have experience in a leadership role and have exceptional communication skills for interactions with the public, partnering agencies, and with SIU staff. Must be able to create a work schedule and delegate tasks. 

How to Apply:

Please email a cover letter, CV, and three references combined into a single PDF to Tadao Kishimoto at tadao.kishimoto@siu.edu.

For technician applicants, name the PDF and use the email subject line:
 YourLastName_deertech_2027
 (e.g., Kishimoto_deertech_2027)

For lead technician applicants, add “_lead” to both the PDF name and email subject line:
 YourLastName_deertech_2027_lead
 (e.g., Kishimoto_deertech_2027_lead)

In the body of the email, please state your position preference (technician or lead technician), preferred start date (November 18 or January 4), and your availability through the remainder of the field season.

Contact
Tadao Kishimoto
Tadao.kishimoto@siu.edu (preferred contact method)

Description
We are hiring one (1) seasonal Wildlife Technician to assist with a project surveying for plains spotted skunks and other mesocarnivores in southeastern Oklahoma from ~January 12 through ~May 7, 2027. Spotted skunks are rare and elusive mesocarnivores that were recently petitioned to be listed under the Endangered Species Act. This study continues and expands upon research on plains spotted skunk population ecology and landcover associations conducted since 2023 (See Brosend et al. 2026 in Wildlife Biology).  The selected candidate will work closely with a graduate student to conduct camera surveys and live trapping for plains spotted skunks and possible side projects related to the study. The selected candidate must be able and willing to hike long distances (up to 20 km per day), over difficult terrain, in potentially extreme conditions (e.g., both cold winter conditions and warm spring temperatures and humidity). The use of olfactory lures is a daily occurrence and those with sensitivities to unsavory smells should consider this when applying. Additionally, candidates with a current rabies vaccine, live-capture experience and previous animal handling experience are encouraged to apply, though these skills are not necessary and those without will not be penalized during the selection process. Attention to detail, a good attitude, and a good work ethic are essential for this position! The selected candidate should anticipate, and be comfortable with, having limited connectivity (i.e., internet or cellular service) and shared (potentially co-ed) living conditions in a small cabin (or similar accommodations). 

Minimum Qualifications:

• Progress towards a bachelor’s degree in wildlife ecology, biology, ecology, or closely related field

• Ability to lift and carry over 50 pounds

• Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate with coworkers and supervisors

• Ability to maintain a positive and mature attitude and good sense of humor, even under harsh, inclement, or uncomfortable conditions (e.g., inclement weather, biting insects, venomous snakes)

• ≥6 months of field experience with wildlife surveys, demonstrating an ability to work in a remote setting and hike over difficult terrain

• Highly motivated with a strong work ethic

• A valid US driver’s license (without restrictions)

Desired Qualifications:

• B.S. in wildlife management, natural resources, or a closely related discipline

• Experience using camera traps to monitor wildlife as part of an ecological study

• Experience running trap lines with box traps

• Experience driving pickup trucks with and without a trailer attached, and/or in 4WD

To apply: Please combine the following into a single PDF file as “YourName_OSUSkunks: (1) a single-page cover letter that details why you are interested in this position, your most relevant experiences, and your professional goals/aspirations; (2) a Curriculum Vitae; and (3) contact information (i.e., name, affiliation, email, and phone number) for 3 references. Send the PDF file as an attachment to Danielle.brosend@okstate.edu no later than 16 October 2026 with the subject titled “Skunk Tech Position”. Please note that applications may be reviewed as they are received and a candidate may be selected before the closing date of 16 October 2026. Electronic (email) submission of applications is encouraged but mail is also fine; mailed applications should be postmarked by 16 October 2026 and sent to Danielle Brosend - OSU NREM, 320G Agricultural Hall, Stillwater, OK 74078.

Oklahoma State University (OSU) is located in Stillwater, Oklahoma, which is within an hour of both Tulsa and Oklahoma City. OSU is a land-grant institution with an enrollment of ~25,000 students, and it is located on the ancestral lands of the Kickapoo, Osage, Kiowa, and Quapaw peoples. Indigenous people from other Native nations also reside here, many of whom were forcibly removed from their ancestral lands. They all contribute to the history and current vitality of our region. The Department of Natural Resource Ecology and Management is part of the Division of Agricultural Sciences and Natural Resources and conducts interdisciplinary research, instruction, and extension education to address the sustainable management and conservation of the wildlife, forest, rangeland, and fishery resources of Oklahoma and beyond. The Department is a source of cutting-edge research, quality instruction, and effective outreach to students, landowners, managers, and public agencies.

Description
 ROCKY MOUNTAIN YOUTH CORPS
Conservation Program Coordinator 
Upper Rio Grande Office (Taos)

Rocky Mountain Youth Corps (RMYC) is a nonprofit youth development organization serving New Mexico. We inspire young adults to make a positive difference in themselves and their communities. Through training and service, Corpsmembers discover their potential for healthy, productive lives.


Position Title: Conservation Program Coordinator, Upper Rio Grande Region
Position Timeline: Targeted start date is November 2026 
Work Location: Taos, NM, with travel throughout the state
                             1321 Salazar Rd, Taos, New Mexico 87571 
Classification:  Full-time, Salaried Exempt
Schedule: The position follows a seasonal schedule that varies based on program operations and needs.
Spring: Primarily spike schedule (Tuesday - Tuesday, eight 10 hour days) with additional office days as needed 
Summer and Fall: Primarily Monday–Friday, with early starts and late ends during rig-up and de-rig days. Additional hours outside a typical work schedule are often required for project completion, incident response, and other operational needs.
Winter: Monday–Friday
Compensation: Starting range is $47,840 to $54,080 ($23-$26/hr); All benefits as provided for in RMYC staff manual, after a 60-day waiting period, including Health/Dental insurance (100% of premiums for staff covered by RMYC), over 19 days of PTO,  14 paid holidays, 3% match to SIMPLE IRA, Life Insurance, Flexible Spending Account, Employee Assistance Program, annual wellness benefit and access to pro-deals.
Supervision Exercised: Exercises supervision over Crew Supervisors and Field Technicians. Provides substantial indirect supervision of Assistant Crew Leads & Crew Members
Supervision Received: Receives general supervision from the Upper Rio Grande Program Manager; indirect supervision by Conservation Program Director and Executive Director 

Position Summary: The Conservation Program Coordinator serves as a central point of coordination for program execution, connecting RMYC program staff, Crew Supervisors, Corpsmembers, and project partners to ensure that crews are prepared, supported, and operating safely and effectively throughout every aspect of the program year. The Coordinator serves as a primary point of contact and resource for Crew Supervisors and Members, providing guidance, problem-solving, training, and coordination across the full range of program needs. The Conservation Program Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that planning and technical needs are fully addressed, drawing on broad conservation knowledge and problem-solving skills. The Coordinator provides field-based technical leadership, trains crews in conservation practices, monitors project quality and progress, adapts plans to address changing conditions and challenges, and serves as a key resource for risk management and incident response. The Coordinator plays a meaningful role in shaping the culture, standards, and direction of the conservation program. The role requires a strong and steady leadership presence, someone who is engaged and approachable, remains calm and effective when challenges arise, and provides clear direction. The Coordinator must be technically credible and thoughtful in their decision-making, with the adaptability and interpersonal skills to lead in the field, and foster a supportive and accountable team culture. 

Major Responsibilities
Program & Project Operations
Coordinate the successful delivery of conservation projects based out of RMYC’s Upper Rio Grande office from project setup through completion, ensuring projects are effectively planned, resourced, staffed, implemented, and completed to RMYC and partner expectations.
Serve as a central point of coordination among RMYC program staff, Crew Supervisors, Corpsmembers, and project partners throughout project preparation, implementation, and closeout.
Translate project plans into effective field implementation in close coordination with the Project Manager.
Monitor project progress and crew needs continuously, responding to emerging challenges and providing hands-on operational support throughout the season.


Orientation & Training
Design and deliver seasonal orientation intensive that prepares staff and Corpsmembers to safely and effectively carry out their roles and conservation projects.
Develop and adapt training curriculum based on program requirements and crew-specific needs, incorporating technical conservation skills, crew leadership and management, safety and risk management, youth development, and program practices.
Coordinate and facilitate training delivery, including instructors, locations, schedules, curriculum, logistics, and hands-on instruction.
Provide ongoing field training and technical support throughout project delivery, adapting instruction as crews encounter unfamiliar practices, equipment, or site conditions.

Safety, Risk Management & Incident Response
Integrate safety and risk management into program planning, decision-making, training, and field operations.
Serve as the primary program resource for assessing and managing risk associated with field operations 
Respond to incidents and emerging safety concerns, coordinating appropriate support and intervention as needed.

Field Operations
Provide hands-on field leadership and operational support to ensure crews have the resources, coverage, and logistical support needed to succeed.
Provide temporary or extended field coverage when staffing needs require, including assuming Crew Supervisor responsibilities at project locations across New Mexico for periods ranging from individual days to multiple weeks.
Support project logistics and field coordination across project locations in New Mexico.

Crew Personnel Coordination
Lead the recruitment, hiring, onboarding, and personnel processes for Crew Supervisors, Assistant Crew Leaders, and Corpsmembers.
Manage ongoing personnel and administrative processes throughout the season, ensuring required documentation, records, changes, and other personnel requirements are completed accurately, consistently, and on time.

Corpsmember Support & Development
Provide ongoing support and guidance to Corpsmembers, serving as a trusted point of contact for wellness, development, sometimes in challenging or sensitive situations.
Respond to Corpsmember needs throughout the season, helping participants navigate personal, interpersonal, and program-related challenges.
Provide timely support and intervention when urgent or emerging needs arise, including situations requiring immediate travel or response outside of regular working hours.

Other Responsibilities
Support Project Manager in partner outreach and project generation and planning 
Update Project Impact database with measurable results of crew work; complete regular crew/project reporting in compliance with all grant/agreement requirements.
Assist the Program Manager in developing and implementing new program initiatives and long-term planning.
Assist crew supervisors in tracking and coding all projects, expenses, and in-kind contributions. Track service hours for AmeriCorps members and work with individuals to ensure they complete the required number of service hours.
Review and approve timecards for accuracy, and ensure timely submission.
Provide training in data collection and monitoring related to forest health, trail maintenance, habitat improvement, and other project or program requirements, including the use of Survey123, Avenza, georeferenced PDFs, QGIS, and ArcGIS Pro/ArcGIS Online. 
Serve as a rotating member of On Call team for after-hours and weekend field support and incident response related to both Upper Rio Grande and Middle Rio Grande crews.
Work closely with the Logistics Coordinator and Program Manager to ensure the timely procurement and delivery of tools, equipment, and supplies needed to successfully complete field projects.
Provide training, logistical support, and on-the-ground coordination for crews during disaster response deployments.
Other duties as assigned.


Job Requirements:
Exceptional leadership, emotional maturity, and sound judgment, with the ability to remain calm and effective in challenging situations, build trust with diverse Corpsmembers and staff, set clear expectations, and provide consistent support, mentorship, and accountability.
Exceptional communication, teaching, and facilitation skills, with the ability to engage and lead groups, clearly convey technical concepts, and adapt instruction to different levels of experience and learning styles.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to assess complex and unexpected situations, develop practical solutions, and respond effectively to challenges in the field and across program operations.
Strong knowledge and familiarity with current conservation initiatives, especially in New Mexico and the American Southwest.
Demonstrated understanding of the public land managing agencies operating in New Mexico, such as the Bureau of Land Management, U.S. Forest Service, National Park Service, Bureau of Reclamation, New Mexico State Land Office, and New Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department.
Strong understanding of recreation and natural resource management principles and practices, including ecological restoration, forest monitoring, prescribed fire, and invasive species management and removal, with the ability to apply this knowledge effectively in the field. 
Strong technical field skills, including chainsaw operation, trail construction and maintenance, fencing, hand tool use and maintenance, basic carpentry, and heavy equipment operation.
Demonstrated proficiency in off-road driving.

Qualifications:
Minimum two years of field experience in natural resource management, outdoor education, or related fields.
Minimum one year of experience with a Youth/Conservation Corps or other program serving youth and young adults.
High School Diploma or equivalent (Preferred: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution).
Wilderness First Responder (WFR) or higher medical certification, or ability to obtain WFR within 3 months.
Minimum 21 years of age, with valid driver’s license and insurable motor vehicle record.
Pre-employment background check will be required, including an FBI fingerprint background check.
B-level (FalB) or equivalent sawyer certification from a United States Forest Service-approved training program, or ability to obtain such certification within 3 months.
(Preferred) Leave No Trace Master Educator or Trainer certification.
(Preferred) First Aid/CPR Instructor certification.

Working Conditions:
In performing the essential functions of this position, the Conservation Program Coordinator will be required to:
Operate standard office equipment, telephones, and computers.
Lift or move up to 50 pounds occasionally, up to 20 pounds frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds constantly.
Traverse uneven terrain and perform physical activities including balancing, stooping, kneeling, reaching, pushing, pulling, and grasping.
Work outdoors in variable environmental conditions and around occasional loud equipment such as chainsaws.
Occasionally hike long distances carrying gear and equipment weighing 50-60 pounds.
Have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles and determine accuracy, and thoroughness of work assigned.
Receive detailed information through oral communication; convey spoken instructions accurately and effectively.

Reasonable accommodations may be made for qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Travel Requirements:
The Conservation Program Coordinator must be available to travel as needed to remote project locations throughout New Mexico and be prepared to camp overnight for multiple nights, both near vehicles and in backcountry settings. In the case of disaster response deployments, the Conservation Program Coordinator may be required to remain on site (including out-of-state locations) for extended periods of time, up to 30 days.

Rocky Mountain Youth Corps is available to all and we will not discriminate or refuse services to any staff or member because of perceived or actual race, color, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, political affiliation, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital or parental status, military service or pregnancy.

RMYC is a drug free workplace.  All RMYC positions depend upon funding availability.

To apply, visit www.youthcorps.org. For additional questions, please contact Chandler Callahan, Upper Rio Grande Conservation Program Manager (chandler@youthcorps.org)

Description
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting candidates to fill the role of a Data Management Specialist in the Alaska Marine Mammal Observer Program. This is a full-year, full-time benefits-eligible position with an expected start date of November 15th, 2026.
 
In southeastern Alaska, mortality and serious injury of harbor porpoise incidental to the salmon drift gillnet fishery is of conservation concern. The person hired for this position will work collaboratively with staff from Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission (PSMFC), the National Marine Fisheries Service Alaska Fisheries Science Center (NMFS AFSC), State of Alaska, and industry members of the SE Alaska gillnet fleet implement and manage an electronic monitoring program to document marine mammal interactions (Alaska Marine Mammal Observation Program, or AMMOP).  In its initial years, this new EM program will collect data required to evaluate harbor porpoise mortality incidental to the state-managed salmon drift gillnet fishery operating within the inland waters of southeastern Alaska. The overarching goal of the project is to design and implement a monitoring program which will provide comprehensive assessment of protected species bycatch.
 
Our initial scoping phase was implemented in 2024 and 2025 to help us gain knowledge about the SE Alaska drift gillnet fishery, assess logistics involved in the collection of statistically reliable information using electronic monitoring. The continuing scoping years (2026 and beyond) are focused on optimizing the tools necessary to support a long-term scalable electronic monitoring program, responsive to management needs.
 
We are seeking a person who is a self-starter, can work well with diverse stakeholders, and is proactive and flexible.  This person will be key to getting vessels recruited to the electronic monitoring program and building the relationships with industry so that this is a collaborative and mutually beneficial program.
 
Position Duties:
Coordinate with vessels and electronic monitoring (EM) equipment provider (vendor) to get equipment on vessels and operational during 2027.
Coordinate with AFSC staff on the PSMFC development of communications and training materials, data workflow, database, and data QA/QC processes.
Support the administrative obligations of the project (supporting the leads at PSMFC and NMFS), including budget management, equipment acquisition, and other related duties.
Write, edit, and assemble progress reports on achievement of project deliverables; contribute to technical reports and annual reports, as requested and as required by fiscal and grant award reporting guidelines.
Represent the AMMOP project and PSMFC in meetings with agencies (federal and state), tribes, fishing industry representatives, universities, and consultants. Coordinate activities with affected parties and gain support and acceptance of proposals and recommendations.
Knowledge Required by the Position:

The successful candidate will require strong communication, collaboration, facilitation and leadership skills, as well as data analysis and project management skills related to the natural sciences. Key attributes include but are not limited to:

Knowledge of principles, methods, techniques, and systems of project management. This includes the ability to provide support to leadership in the areas of:
goal setting, budgeting, direction of personnel, travel management, time and attendance management, procurement, contract administration
Ability to apply sound judgment in the solution of organizational and operational problems in a timely, economical fashion.
Ability to analyze and summarize data for reporting to a diverse set of stakeholders.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with all levels of key management, staff, government agencies, and private concerns. This requires tact, ingenuity, and resourcefulness.
Ability to communicate effectively, in both written and oral form, with individuals and groups having diverse backgrounds and technical expertise.
Knowledge of data and data systems:
computers and software packages and applications for databases, spreadsheets, and word processing
data management concepts, principles, and methods
quality assurance principles
technical documentation methods and procedures
analytical methods and common query languages
the organization's data sets sufficient to: 
input data; structure information retrievals;
edit, combine and manipulate data; and/or provide reports for users. 
Essential Functions relative to data management: 

At the lower end of the range, Data Management Specialists (Natural Sciences):

Compile project data into standardized electronic data formats. This includes accessing filed information and verifying its accuracy and completeness, performing data entry, electronic data transfer, editing, and error checking.
Extract relevant data which may be presented in many different text and numeric formats, reports, tables, graphics, or figures.
Maintain local versions of datasets in accordance with established regional database exchange formats and standards.
Maintain a local archive of current and historical reports and documents. Coordinate the regular transfer of reference materials to archives and libraries.
Train technical and general users in the use of database applications through individual instruction and/or group presentations.
Create queries, summaries, and/or maps in response to requests for customized data.
Prepare and manipulate various data and graphic outputs for use in reports, presentations and internet applications using standardized retrieval scripts.
At the upper end of the range, employees:

Develop and implement databases and libraries. Includes acquiring new data as well as taking previously created or historical databases or spreadsheets and integrating them. Data sources vary in format including database, spreadsheet, and survey data sets. Custom interfaces may be required.
Produce written research and statistical reports (including graphs, tables, maps, and text), data sets, and data summaries using a variety of analytical techniques and software tools. This involves the master-level use of database retrieval scripts.
Document data handling and reporting to ensure consistency and validity of data between and within sites. Files may come from sources that use different computer hardware, software systems/protocols, and different communication packages.
Maintain and update data catalogs, data catalog directories, and metadata.
Perform system maintenance and backups. This includes routine database checkpoints, checkpoint verification, tuning, data-process merges, and user account management. Restore files when required.
Perform Help Desk functions, responding to on-line user inquiries about access to the database and data retrievals, the execution of query scripts, and standard report programs.
 

Supervisory Controls:

Work is assigned in terms of project goals, objectives, priorities, and, at times, specific tasks.  At the lower end of the range, the employee will exercise initiative in solving common technical and procedural problems.  Unusual issues are referred to the supervisor or higher-graded employee for consultation or review. 

At the upper end of the range, the employee plans and carries out assignments with independence, guided by experience and knowledge to complete the objective.  He/she seeks assistance only on the most unusual issues. Sufficiency of planning and execution, and accuracy of the data produced are normally accepted without detailed review, even for customized assignments.

 

Guidelines:

Guidelines include PSMFC standards and policies; project work plans; data submission protocol documents; established database structures, data definitions, and data standards; and various hardware and software manuals. 

At the lower end of the range, the guidelines are clear and provide little room for deviation, except as provided in documented precedents or suggestions for alternative data entry and retrieval strategies.  New or revised job requirements or requests for data that cannot be processed within the existing guidelines are discussed with the supervisor or higher level employee.

At the higher end of the range, the employee reviews each work request and selects and interprets guidelines to achieve the desired end product.   

 

Complexity:

At the lower end of the range, the employee decides what to do by identifying the data content and information structure needed for each processing request and selecting the appropriate routine to set up and format each job. 

At the higher end of the range, data will be in any number of formats.  Computerized data may not be in a form that matches user needs exactly and therefore requires translation into a common format.  Data may be missing or in a format that requires conversion to defined standards.

 

Scope and Effect:

A high quality, consistent set of biological and geographical data is necessary for effective policy setting, planning, management and research.  Data must be provided in an efficient and timely manner, and in a format that meets the needs of users.

 

Personal Contacts:

Contacts are with employees in PSMFC; federal, state, or tribal agencies; university researchers, private/non-profit organizations, and the general public.

 

Purpose of Contacts:

The purpose of the contacts is to exchange information and insure that project goals are being met through coordination, planning, and mutual support.  Communication between contacts resolves problems with data; affords the exchange of information, ideas, and concepts; and allows for the acquisition of products and information. 

 

Physical Demands:

The work is a mix of sedentary office work and field coordination in harbors and ports.  This requires the ability to navigate on wet and slippery docks and harbor walkways, walk moderate distances.  There are light carrying loads (papers, books, reports, etc.) that require only moderate physical ability and physical stress.

requirements:
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting candidates to fill the role of a Data Management Specialist in the Alaska Marine Mammal Observer Program. This is a full-year, full-time benefits-eligible position with an expected start date of November 15th, 2026.
 
In southeastern Alaska, mortality and serious injury of harbor porpoise incidental to the salmon drift gillnet fishery is of conservation concern. The person hired for this position will work collaboratively with staff from Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission (PSMFC), the National Marine Fisheries Service Alaska Fisheries Science Center (NMFS AFSC), State of Alaska, and industry members of the SE Alaska gillnet fleet implement and manage an electronic monitoring program to document marine mammal interactions (Alaska Marine Mammal Observation Program, or AMMOP).  In its initial years, this new EM program will collect data required to evaluate harbor porpoise mortality incidental to the state-managed salmon drift gillnet fishery operating within the inland waters of southeastern Alaska. The overarching goal of the project is to design and implement a monitoring program which will provide comprehensive assessment of protected species bycatch.
 
Our initial scoping phase was implemented in 2024 and 2025 to help us gain knowledge about the SE Alaska drift gillnet fishery, assess logistics involved in the collection of statistically reliable information using electronic monitoring. The continuing scoping years (2026 and beyond) are focused on optimizing the tools necessary to support a long-term scalable electronic monitoring program, responsive to management needs.
 
We are seeking a person who is a self-starter, can work well with diverse stakeholders, and is proactive and flexible.  This person will be key to getting vessels recruited to the electronic monitoring program and building the relationships with industry so that this is a collaborative and mutually beneficial program.
 
Position Duties:
Coordinate with vessels and electronic monitoring (EM) equipment provider (vendor) to get equipment on vessels and operational during 2027.
Coordinate with AFSC staff on the PSMFC development of communications and training materials, data workflow, database, and data QA/QC processes.
Support the administrative obligations of the project (supporting the leads at PSMFC and NMFS), including budget management, equipment acquisition, and other related duties.
Write, edit, and assemble progress reports on achievement of project deliverables; contribute to technical reports and annual reports, as requested and as required by fiscal and grant award reporting guidelines.
Represent the AMMOP project and PSMFC in meetings with agencies (federal and state), tribes, fishing industry representatives, universities, and consultants. Coordinate activities with affected parties and gain support and acceptance of proposals and recommendations.
Knowledge Required by the Position:

The successful candidate will require strong communication, collaboration, facilitation and leadership skills, as well as data analysis and project management skills related to the natural sciences. Key attributes include but are not limited to:

Knowledge of principles, methods, techniques, and systems of project management. This includes the ability to provide support to leadership in the areas of:
goal setting, budgeting, direction of personnel, travel management, time and attendance management, procurement, contract administration
Ability to apply sound judgment in the solution of organizational and operational problems in a timely, economical fashion.
Ability to analyze and summarize data for reporting to a diverse set of stakeholders.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with all levels of key management, staff, government agencies, and private concerns. This requires tact, ingenuity, and resourcefulness.
Ability to communicate effectively, in both written and oral form, with individuals and groups having diverse backgrounds and technical expertise.
Knowledge of data and data systems:
computers and software packages and applications for databases, spreadsheets, and word processing
data management concepts, principles, and methods
quality assurance principles
technical documentation methods and procedures
analytical methods and common query languages
the organization's data sets sufficient to: 
input data; structure information retrievals;
edit, combine and manipulate data; and/or provide reports for users. 
Essential Functions relative to data management: 

At the lower end of the range, Data Management Specialists (Natural Sciences):

Compile project data into standardized electronic data formats. This includes accessing filed information and verifying its accuracy and completeness, performing data entry, electronic data transfer, editing, and error checking.
Extract relevant data which may be presented in many different text and numeric formats, reports, tables, graphics, or figures.
Maintain local versions of datasets in accordance with established regional database exchange formats and standards.
Maintain a local archive of current and historical reports and documents. Coordinate the regular transfer of reference materials to archives and libraries.
Train technical and general users in the use of database applications through individual instruction and/or group presentations.
Create queries, summaries, and/or maps in response to requests for customized data.
Prepare and manipulate various data and graphic outputs for use in reports, presentations and internet applications using standardized retrieval scripts.

Description
 POSTDOCTORAL FELLOW
 
 The Department of Natural Resource Ecology and Management in the Division of Agricultural Sciences and Natural Resources at Oklahoma State University invites applications for the position of Postdoctoral Fellow (applications can be submitted at the OSU posting for this position here: https://jobs.okstate.edu/jobs/postdoc-fellow-for-migratory-bird-research-bf9454-stillwater-oklahoma-united-states).

Position Description

Funding is available for a two-year postdoctoral research position to work with Drs. Craig Davis and Scott Loss in the Department of Natural Resource Ecology and Management (NREM) at Oklahoma State University. This position is funded through the South Central Climate Adaptation Science Center (SC-CASC) and will address research questions related to the impacts of climate change on migratory birds and their habitats in the U.S. Great Plains region. The postdoc will lead work that expands on our previous research evaluating effects of changing precipitation regimes on wetland extent and migratory waterbird habitat use in the Great Plains. Specifically, the postdoctoral fellow will: (1) use existing datasets and analysis results to develop and publish a user-informed decision support tool that stakeholders can use to prioritize wetland management strategies that increase resilience of wetlands and waterbirds to climate change, and (2) leverage existing datasets on bird habitat use and movements to evaluate climate change effects on habitat, movements, and/or migration phenology for birds in the Great Plains region.

Well-qualified individuals with a strong quantitative modeling background, experience working with large data sets, and research interests in climate effects on avian species and their habitat are encouraged to apply. Experience with decision support tools is also beneficial but not required. In addition to collaborating with Drs. Davis and Loss, the postdoc will collaborate with an interdisciplinary research team that includes: Dr. Omkar Joshi (a social scientist in NREM); past and current OSU graduate students and postdocs funded on the same project; and project stakeholders and partners with state, federal, and tribal agencies.

As one of several postdoctoral researchers working across the SC-CASC consortium, the postdoc will also contribute to leadership and research support activities that assist the SC-CASC’s mission and deliverables and will be a part of the CASC’s Research Scholars Program, which will provide further collaboration and professional development opportunities.       

Salary Information

Salary for this postdoctoral fellow position is $60,000/yr plus benefits excluding retirement; funding is also available for travel to meet with collaborators and present at scientific conferences.  Check out our competitive benefits and eligibility at https://hr.okstate.edu/prospective-ee.html

Employment Conditions

This is an 11-month temporary faculty position (but note that funding for a 12th month is also typically available). Appointments are to be made for a term of one year or less.  Reappointments for a total period of not more than two years may be made. Review of applications will begin October 30, 2026, and will continue until a suitable applicant is identified. Anticipated start date is between November 2026 and Jan 2027 (start date is somewhat flexible).

Qualifications

Applicants must have a Ph.D. in ecology, conservation biology, natural resource management, or a related field; demonstrated experience conducting research that results in peer-reviewed publications; strong quantitative analysis skills including past experience managing and analyzing large data sets; strong written and oral communications skills; and a strong record of successfully leading and participating in collaborative team research. Ideal candidates will also have prior experience working with or alongside federal agencies, and a genuine interest in conducting actionable and co-produced science.

Application

Applications must be submitted online at: https://jobs.okstate.edu; specific job posting is here: https://jobs.okstate.edu/jobs/postdoc-fellow-for-migratory-bird-research-bf9454-stillwater-oklahoma-united-states)
 
Applicants should submit: 1) a cover letter summarizing their experience and research expertise related to the above project goals and required qualifications, 2) curriculum vitae, and 3) contact information for three references. 

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION, PLEASE CONTACT:
 
 Dr. Craig Davis or Dr. Scott Loss
 Oklahoma State University
 Department of Natural Resource Ecology and Management
 Email: craig.a.davis@okstate.edu or scott.loss@okstate.edu
 http://nrem.okstate.edu

 The Department of Natural Resource Ecology & Management provides instruction, research and Extension expertise that focuses on the natural resources of fisheries, forests, rangeland and wildlife within and beyond the boundaries of Oklahoma Our mission is to increase public awareness and understanding through teaching, research and Extension, of the ecology, management and sustainable use of these natural resources that are important for maintaining ecosystem health, species diversity, agriculture and forest production, hunting and fishing, and the enjoyment of experiencing nature. Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a SEPA and Environmental Regulation Specialist (Environmental Specialist 3) within the Nuclear Waste Program.

Location: 
Richland Field Office in Richland, WA. 
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule: 
Initially, this position requires working in the office five days a week for onboarding and training. Flexible schedule options are available. 
Upon successful completion of the probationary period, a primarily telework schedule may be established with supervisor approval, based on position needs.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline:
Apply by October 14, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

Join the Nuclear Waste Program’s Compliance and Regulatory Assistance team as a State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) and Environmental Regulation Specialist, where your work will help protect human health and Washington’s environmental resources for future generations. In this role, you will be responsible for leading technical reviews and coordination under the SEPA, National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA), and other environmental regulations. Working closely with managers, engineers, scientists, legal staff, and external partners, you will evaluate diverse and complex environmental projects, identify key issues, and ensure regulatory compliance that supports long-term protection of the environment.

This position provides meaningful opportunities to expand your technical expertise while contributing to environmental planning, cleanup activities, and policy development across the Nuclear Waste Program.

What you will do:
Evaluate SEPA, NEPA, MTCA, and other regulatory notifications to identify environmental issues and ensure compliance with state and federal requirements. 
Prepare, review, and coordinate SEPA documentation, including administrative records, Categorical Exclusions, Environmental Assessments, Environmental Impact Statements, Supplemental Analyses, and related technical materials.
Manage, sort, and file all documents in established databases and record keeping systems.
Provide technical and programmatic support for environmental planning and compliance activities under state and federal regulations, including performing technical analysis and review of impacts on the environment. 
Collaborate with project managers, engineers, scientists, environmental specialists, legal staff, and agency staff to collect data, clarify regulatory requirements, and facilitate environmental reviews. 
Apply strong communication, organizational, analytical, and project management skills to support multiple projects while ensuring regulatory compliance and schedule adherence. 
Track project schedules, milestones, deliverables, and action items to ensure timely completion and effective coordination.


Qualifications


For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website.


Required Qualifications:

Six (6) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which must include the following:
Environmental Policy Experience – Ability to apply knowledge of environmental policy frameworks, including SEPA, NEPA, and other laws and regulations, to evaluate proposals and guide staff and agencies to ensure consistent, accurate, and legally defensible environmental decision-making.
Scientific and Technical Analysis – Ability to apply scientific and regulatory analytical methods to evaluate documents to determine environmental impacts and support defensible agency decisions.
Regulatory Interpretation – Ability to interpret complex environmental regulations to provide accurate guidance to staff and external partners to ensure consistent regulatory compliance.
Data Analysis – Ability to analyze environmental data, records, and regulatory information to ensure accurate interpretation, support environmental impact assessments, and improve the quality and reliability of environmental decision-making.
Conflict Resolution & Integration – Ability to reconcile differing technical perspectives across programs to develop unified, scientifically supported recommendations that improve cross-program regulatory alignment.
Project Coordination – Ability to coordinate environmental review schedules and tasks to ensure timely completion of deliverables and compliance with program requirements.
Software & Tools – Ability to operate standard and specialized software (Microsoft Office Suite, Outlook, SharePoint, Adobe, environmental tracking systems) to produce accurate documentation, run queries, conduct analysis, and distribute information efficiently.

Education involving a major study in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; environmental or natural science interdisciplinary studies; environmental planning, or closely related field.


Examples of how to qualify:
6 years of experience.
5 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
4 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
3 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
2 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
Master’s degree or higher.

Workload Experience: Experience planning work and organizing documents.
Regulatory Compliance: Ability to interpret state, federal, and local environmental regulations (e.g., SEPA, NEPA, MTCA, CERCLA, RCRA, ESA, CWA, CAA, AEA, NWPA, SDWA, TSCA, EPCRA) to ensure correct application of requirements and support for consistent, lawful environmental decision-making.
Environmental and Resource Management: Knowledge of principles, practices, and methods of environmental or resource management and environmental pollution prevention and pollution control; methods and techniques of field sampling, testing, data gathering, basic research, and field investigations; technical report writing methods; and characteristics and health effects of pollutants.
